name_note: GTDB splits the classical species Anaerostipes hadrus into several genome-based species; hadrus_C is one of them, so published findings on Anaerostipes hadrus may cover a broader group.

sentences.text: Anaerostipes hadrus was proposed as a new combination transferring Eubacterium hadrum to the genus Anaerostipes, within the family Lachnospiraceae.

The strains studied were isolated as D-lactate-utilizing bacteria from faecal samples of a healthy individual, and the species description was expanded to include butyrate production from D-lactate and acetate.
A genomic study described Anaerostipes hadrus as a dominant species in the human gut microbiota and found 5-fluorouracil metabolism genes as ubiquitous in its genomes as butyrate-producing genes.
The same study reported a wide and stable distribution in healthy individuals, patients with inflammatory bowel disease and patients with colorectal cancer, with healthy individuals carrying more.

Another study reported that isolates of this butyrate-producing Lachnospiraceae member show strain-specific patterns of nutrient niche access, and that strain-specific carbohydrate use drives variable short-chain fatty acid production.
